text:
anna (support): Customer reports intermittent 500s + `RuntimeError: Event loop is closed` when using our Python SDK from a background thread. They say it happens mostly during token refresh and heavy retry windows.

mike (eng): Which sdk/httpx versions? Any minimal repro? :eyes:

anna (support): redwood-python 0.14.2, httpx 0.23.3, uvicorn 0.18. Repro is a simple background thread that calls the sync wrapper `Client()` from startup.

tyler (platform): paste the repro (short) so we can run it locally.

anna (support): sure — minimal: 
```python
from redwood import Client
import threading

c = Client(api_key="REDACTED")

def background():
    # using SDK sync wrapper from a plain thread
    resp = c.chat.create("Hello")
    print(resp)

thr = threading.Thread(target=background)
thr.start()
thr.join()
```

anna (support): customer logs show repeated retry attempts then the trace: `RuntimeError: Event loop is closed` and then 500 responses from our API when token refresh fails under concurrency.

mike (eng): stack excerpt?

anna (support):
```
File "/.../site-packages/httpx/_client.py", line 1498, in request
  await self._transport.handle_async_request(...)
RuntimeError: Event loop is closed
```

mike (eng): Thanks. Guess: sync wrapper ends up running async token-refresh logic using `asyncio.run` or similar. In background threads there isn't a main running loop; depending on Python runtime/shutdown sequence `asyncio.get_event_loop()`/`get_running_loop()` can behave unexpectedly and you end up scheduling/running coroutines against a loop that gets closed. Also our retry/backoff queues can amplify the number of concurrent refresh attempts, exhausting resources and triggering more 500s.

tyler (platform): I can reproduce locally by spawning many threads that call the sync API at shutdown time. Repro leads to loop closed or frozen threads.

mike (eng): Short-term mitigations to suggest to customers:
- Avoid calling the sync wrapper from background threads. Initialize and call from the main thread, or use proper async code.
- Use explicit async client usage: `async with Client() as c: await c.chat.create(...)` in an event loop you control.
- If they must use threads, ensure they don't call during process shutdown and upgrade httpx to the latest patch (0.24.x) which has a couple of edge-case fixes.

anna (support): Sent that workaround. They asked for a patch ETA.

mike (eng): We'll add a defensive check in the next SDK release: detect calls from non-main threads with no running loop and raise a clear error message explaining the cause + recommended fix. Also reduce simultaneous refresh attempts by coalescing token refreshes (single-flight). I'll open an issue and a patch.

devops-bot: issue #1456 created by mike -> https://github.com/redwood/inference/issues/1456 :detect-sync-in-thread-eventloop

mike (eng): Additionally recommend setting an environment flag (internal): `REDWOOD_SYNC_IN_THREAD=error` to force early failure for affected clients until patch ships. We'll include a migration note in the changelog.

tyler (platform): Also keep an eye on billing/metrics — retry storms will inflate request counts. We should backfill alert graphs and flag customers impacted.

anna (support): I'll update the customer with the workaround, the env flag, and link to the GH issue. I'll mark the case high priority because of the billing spike. :thumbsup:

mike (eng): Plan: PR with detection + single-flight refresh this week, release 0.15.0-next, then ship patch release.

anna (support): great — closing this thread for now, follow-ups in the GH issue.

(THREAD END)
